findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so objects are stored with S3-managed keys (or whatever the account default is) rather than an explicit KMS key, leaving no enforced control over encryption of stored reports data.
No ACL is specified and no public access block or bucket policy restricts access, so the bucket relies on unspecified defaults rather than an explicitly private ACL as used by the sibling buckets.
Versioning is not enabled on reports_archive, so objects overwritten or deleted (including by force_destroy or a compromised principal) cannot be recovered.
No logging block is configured for reports_archive, so access to the reports bucket is not recorded in the audit trail.
The ledger_exports bucket contains financial ledger exports but declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, so encryption is left to defaults rather than an explicit KMS key.
Versioning is not enabled on ledger_exports, allowing ledger objects to be permanently lost or tampered with without a recoverable prior version.
No logging configuration is present on ledger_exports, so reads and writes of ledger data are not captured in the audit bucket.
The model_artifacts bucket stores model artifacts with no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so data is not enforced to be encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key.
The ops_runbooks bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving runbook contents unencrypted by explicit policy.
ops_runbooks does not configure access logging, so access to operational runbooks is not audited.

The audit_trail bucket uses the legacy ACL 'log-delivery-write'; TLS-only and public-access-block enforcement are not configured, and the bucket is the logging target for other buckets, so weakening its posture affects audit integrity.
The seed object (vendor-roster.xlsx) is uploaded without kms_key_id or server-side encryption settings, so the sensitive vendor roster is stored using default encryption only.
